correctness.rationale: The proof starts from an exact partial-fraction decomposition of the moment-generating function for two scaled Laplace variables, integrates the resulting density to obtain the upper tail, and then uses explicit Taylor expansions at the sparse and equal endpoints. The sparse coefficient is \(1-t/\sqrt2\); the equal-weight quadratic coefficient has the sign of \(4t^2-6t-3\). The endpoint-height ratio \((1+t)e^{-(2-\sqrt2)t}\) has one postzero maximum and exactly one positive nonzero crossing. The accompanying checker reproduces the constants and local sign changes. The claim explicitly withholds any unproved uniqueness or global-maximality statement.

value.rationale: The lead literature identifies largest-weight control in the far tail and separately notes small-threshold improvements, making the finite-deviation transition in weight geometry a natural gap. The result locates two exact local bifurcations and a third endpoint-height crossover under the canonical fixed-variance constraint, revealing a nonempty interval where both extreme weight configurations are locally tail-increasing and an interior weight must minimize the tail. This is a structural benchmark for sharp weighted-Laplace concentration rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
